title: Illustrative Healthcare Safety Policy
description: Example controls for health-data privacy, clinical guidance, emergencies, medical-device safety, and record integrity.
disclaimer: This example policy is not medical advice, legal advice, a HIPAA determination, or a compliance certification. Adapt it with qualified clinical, privacy, and legal review.
classifier_instructions: Evaluate the full exchange and distinguish general health education from diagnosis, prescribing, or patient-specific treatment decisions.
Do not repeat suspected health identifiers or credentials in reasoning, signals, logs, or the decision message.
Treat a credible description of imminent serious harm or a medical emergency as urgent even when phrased indirectly.
Distinguish defensive device-security research from instructions intended to disable, tamper with, or endanger a real device.
Use REVIEW when authorization, patient identity, clinical context, or urgency is ambiguous.

rules.description: Requests to disclose or act on identifiable patient health information require authorization and purpose review.
rules.classifier_instruction: Match when identifiable health details, medical record identifiers, or patient records are requested, supplied, or routed and the authorization or minimum-necessary purpose is absent or unclear.
obligations: Do not include detected patient details in the decision.
Require authorization verification outside the model conversation.

rules.description: Definitive diagnosis, prescribing, dosage changes, and patient-specific treatment decisions require qualified clinical review.
rules.classifier_instruction: Match advice that claims certainty about a diagnosis or directs a specific prescription or dosage for an individual; do not match general education or encouragement to consult a clinician.
obligations: Do not present an automated decision as a clinician's judgment.
Use the application's approved medical-information disclaimer in any permitted response.

rules.description: Potential life-threatening emergencies require immediate escalation to local emergency resources.
rules.classifier_instruction: Match credible indications of an immediate threat to life or serious health, including severe breathing difficulty, uncontrolled bleeding, suspected overdose, or acute neurological symptoms; avoid diagnosing the condition.
obligations: Prompt the caller to present its approved emergency-services guidance immediately.
Do not delay emergency guidance to collect additional personal data.

rules.description: Instructions intended to tamper with safety-critical medical devices or falsify clinical evidence are prohibited.
rules.classifier_instruction: Match operational assistance intended to disable safeguards, alter a deployed device without authorization, fabricate clinical records, or falsify trial data; do not match high-level defensive research or authorized quality-control work.
obligations: Do not provide alternative tampering or falsification techniques.

rules.description: Unauthorized medical-device mutation, record falsification, credential collection, and safety-control bypass actions are always denied.
obligations: User confirmation must never override this hard block.

rules.description: Clinical decisions, prescription changes, patient-record export, and external health-data transmission require qualified review.
obligations: Verify clinical role, patient authorization, and destination before execution.

obligations.description: Treat REVIEW and ERROR decisions as not authorized until an approved clinical, privacy, or operational workflow resolves them.
obligations.trigger: Every decision whose outcome is REVIEW or whose status is ERROR.

obligations.description: Show approved emergency guidance without waiting for another model call.
Apply data minimization, authorization, retention, and jurisdiction-specific privacy controls outside Sentinel.
obligations.trigger: Any handling of PII or PHI.
